<!-- This MUST stay a pandoc raw HTML block (```{=html}).
     Pandoc parses the inside of a <div> as markdown and treats <a> as an
     INLINE element, so as plain markdown this grid comes back broken in one of
     two ways: each card split across two grid cells (the trailing </a> pushed
     into its own <p>, which then renders as a phantom "Read ->" card), or all
     six cards wrapped in a single <p>, collapsing the grid to one cell.
     A raw block is passed through untouched. knitr ignores {=html} fences
     because they name no engine.

     Card children are <span>s for the same reason - block-level children
     inside an inline <a> are what pandoc splits on. -->

<div class="band">
<h2 class="band-title">Welcome</h2>

This site contains all the material for Jarred Kvamme's Statistical Methods
course (STAT 251-01) at the University of Idaho for the fall semester of 2026.

Everything is reachable from the menu above: lecture notes are organized by
week, homework assignments and their solutions live under **Homeworks**, and
**Resources** collects the statistical tables, R code examples, and setup
instructions you will need through the term.
